newsitem.title: USA: Gov't grants immunity to tobacco scientist--LA Times.
newsitem.headline: Gov't grants immunity to tobacco scientist--LA Times.

text.p: The U.S. Justice Department has granted immunity to a scientist who allegedly helped tobacco company Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp. develop a plant with high nicotine content, the Los Angeles Times reported Sunday.

The Justic Department has convened grand juries in Washington and New York to consider possible wrongdoing by cigarette makers -- including Brown & Williamson, RJ Reynolds Tobacco Co. and Philip Morris Cos. Inc. -- and it has subpoenaed current and former employees of several companies.

Citing unnamed sources close to the investigation, the Times said Janis Bravo testified at one grand jury that she helped develop a high-nicotine tobacco plant for a joint venture of Brown & Williamson and the company where she worked, DNA Plant Technology.
Bravo did not return calls from the Times seeking comment, and her attorney refused to confirm or deny she had been granted immunity from criminal prosecution if she testified, the newspaper said.

The plant project was first revealed at a congressional hearing in June 1994. At that time, David Kessler, commissioner of the federal Food and Drug Administration, testified the so-called "Y-1" plant had twice as much nicotine by weight as the average U.S. flue-cured tobacco plant. Brown & Williamson executives maintained they were aiming to enhance cigarette flavor.

In 1994, Bravo, whose name was listed on the patent as an inventor of the plant, told FDA investigators that Brown & Williamson already had a high-nicotine gene in its tobacco seed when it hired DNA Plant Technology.

She said her job was to make the plant sterile so that it could not produce more seeds, thus making it harder for competitors to obtain seeds. She also said she shipped some seeds to Brazil before 1991 when a federal law prohibiting the export of tobacco seeds took effect.
Officials at the Justice Department and the FBI declined tocomment to the Times. A Brown & Williamson spokesman said his company does not discuss issues related to grand juries.
RJ Reynolds is a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.
